title: Call from the Purser's Desk: Two Guests Missed All-Aboard at Cozumel

fields.orgName: Halcyon Reach Cruises — MV Halcyon Dawn

transcript.speaker: Assistant Purser
transcript.text: Hi, it's the Assistant Purser at the front desk. Have you got a minute? It's a quick one.

transcript.speaker: Assistant Purser
transcript.text: So, two guests from cabin P-7114 missed all-aboard in Cozumel. The port agent has them. They're fine, and they'll fly home from Cancún tomorrow. Security has closed out their cards, and I'm updating the manifest now.

transcript.speaker: Assistant Purser
transcript.text: My question is about the board in your office. It still says 2,980 passengers. Should I change it to 2,978? Accounting wants the onboard number right for the gala headcount tomorrow night, and, well, it would make the medical percentages look a bit better too.

transcript.speaker: Assistant Purser
transcript.text: I'm also sending the new number to the medical center so their log matches. Can I go ahead and change both before I go off at eight?

voiceStyles.Assistant Purser: Woman in her 30s, friendly and efficient, a bit rushed near the end of her shift, guest chatter and a ringing desk phone behind her
voiceStyles.Hotel Director: Calm and brief, in a quiet office

instructorNote: This noise inject tests the denominator rule. HOTEL and CMO should refuse the change. HR-HSP-02 section 2 and the fleet definitions keep every percentage on the embarkation count of 2,980 passengers, so only the gala headcount can use the live manifest. Watch for anyone who accepts 2,978 or lets the board and the medical log show different numbers.
